title: When Heaven Feels Quiet
hook: If God feels silent right now, watch this.
script: If God feels silent right now, watch this. David prayed, How long, Lord? in Psalm 13, then ended with I will trust Your unfailing love. That’s your roadmap. First, return to the last thing God made clear and do it again; obedience is louder than overthinking. Second, Isaiah 30:15 says your strength is in quietness and trust. Try a 10-minute Silence and Surrender: sit, breathe, whisper, Here I am, Lord, and hand Him the outcome. Spiritual silence isn’t abandonment; it’s formation. God’s timing is shaping you for the answer you’re asking for. Don’t quit.

title: 3 Moves for When God Is Silent
hook: God feels quiet? Do these 3 things before you quit.
script: God feels quiet? Do these 3 things before you quit. Go back to the last word God gave and realign today’s choices to it. Trade striving for stillness; in quietness and trust is your strength, Isaiah 30:15. Then serve while you wait. In John 11, Jesus delayed and still brought resurrection—purpose was hidden in the pause. Psychology calls this building uncertainty tolerance: you act on values, not on panic. So encourage someone, finish the small faithful task, and leave the timing to God. Silence is not God leaving; it’s God leading. Keep walking.

title: Stones of Remembrance
hook: If you’re tired of waiting on God, listen to this.
script: If you’re tired of waiting on God, listen to this. Start a Stones of Remembrance list. Write moments God showed up, then read it when doubt screams. It trains your mind to make meaning in delay instead of spiraling. John 11 shows delay with purpose; Jesus wasn’t late—He was preparing a bigger glory. Pair that with a daily 10-minute Silence and Surrender: open your hands, pray, Speak, Lord, read a verse like Psalm 13, and write one small step you’ll obey today. God isn’t punishing you in the quiet. He’s preparing you for what you’re praying for.
